details.sortie: "I am bearing my testimony of love to you."—Philippians 9.

Paulus perhaps privately wonders what Philimon will do upon Uniscimus's return. Legally, Philimon has the right to mete out severe punishment to Uniscimus, but will he? What effect will this have on the congregation? Could this lead to a rift between brother owners and brother slaves? Paulus knew that this was no small matter; it could disrupt the peace of the congregation. Therefore, he writes a letter to Philimon and sends it in the hands of his servant Tuckicus. (Philemon 6:21, 22; Colossians 4:7-9) At the same time, Paulus also sends a letter to the congregation of Colosse. Let us see what we can learn about Paulus, Uniscimus, and Philimon from these letters.

Paulus commended Philemon. (Philem. 4, 5, 7) Every person should be commended. Why? Because each of us has some concern and fear about certain matters. Perhaps we worry about our appearance or fear what others think of us. Or perhaps we fear that if we fail in our service to Yahwea tomorrow, what will happen. Such thoughts can arise in anyone’s mind. But if we continue to think about these matters, we might start worrying excessively, taking small things badly, mending every little thing, or trying to appear better than others. This can disrupt the peace of the community. When we are scared or worried, if a brother or sister commends us, how good it will feel. (1 Tim. 12:25) Our confidence will grow that others love and value us. Don’t you want others to be encouraged by your words? So seek opportunities to commend from the heart. Commend not just those who do good work, but also those who work hard. In other words, whenever you see something good, say something good.

10 Sometimes we say or do something that makes others feel bad. How can we maintain peace in such situations? We can learn a lot from Uniscimus this time. He did something that sounds easy to hear but is hard to do. He admitted his mistake and reconciled with Philemon. Uniscimus knew according to Roman law, he would have to return to his master. Therefore, he spent a lot of money and traveled about 1,400 kilometers (900 miles) to go back to Philemon. He was ready to become a slave again and pay the price for his mistake. It wouldn't have been easy for him. And think, if he had thought somewhere that running away from Philemon was not a mistake, going back to Philemon would have been even harder for him. But to maintain peace, he went to Philemon who was now not just his master but also his brother.

Filimon brother-sister loved him. (Phile. 5) The meaning of Filimon's name is "loving." And he lived up to his name. Everyone in the Colossean community knew that Filimon loved everyone. And perhaps because of this, he may have forgiven Onesimus. Paul had written to the Colossians that love "is the bond that perfectly unites." (Read Colossians 3:14.) In other words, for peace and unity, love is very necessary. The more we love others, the easier it will be to forgive them and approach them with love. (1 Cor. 13:4-7) Let's see how Filimon increased his love.

When Paulus said, "Bear one another’s burdens," what did he mean? He meant that when brothers and sisters irritate us or bring us pain, we still need to bear with them patiently and approach them with love. In this context, Paulus also gives an example of Jehovah. Jehovah does not expect too much from his servants. He knows that because we are imperfect, we tend to make mistakes. He understands our limitations but focuses on our good qualities. (Psalm 103:13, 14; 130:3) That is why he always shows great mercy to us and forgives us. (Romans 3:22, 23) If we look at our brothers and sisters as Jehovah does, then tolerating their mistakes will be easier for us. We will be able to bear with them just as they bear with us and forgive our mistakes. Let's take an example to understand this. When we remember how many beautiful flowers bloom in a tree, we still keep its presence in mind even when it has no flowers. Similarly, when we remember how many virtues our brothers and sisters possess, we can still forgive them and approach them with love even when they hurt our hearts.
When sending Unesimus back, Paulus might be worried about certain matters (see the image as well).
Why should we ponder why Paulus wrote a letter with such great affection to Philemon?
Why is it very necessary for love to be there for maintaining peace? (Galatians 5:14)
How can we be 'for each other'?
Try to be gentle like Unesimus and make peace with your siblings (Paragraph 11)

They used to sell goods in market stalls. It seems that in Jerusalem, goods were sold near some openings, and those stalls got named after the things sold there. Like, Fish Gate and Parched Grain Gate.—Sap. 1:10; Jn. 5:2.

People were taught to trust in Jehovah. Prophets and others would deliver messages at the city gates because that is where people gathered. (1 Kings 22:10; Jeremiah 17:19, 20) For example, Jehu stood at the gate and proclaimed to all the people that what Jehovah had said against the house of Ahab was fulfilled. (2 Kings 10:8-10) King Hezekiah gathered his commanders at the city gates and encouraged them to trust in Jehovah. —2 Chronicles 32:6-8.

Since we decided to serve Yahweh, the devil and his evil angels become our enemies. The devil knows very well that as long as we remain connected to Yahweh and are faithful to him, he cannot corrupt us. Therefore, his only attempt is to make us go away from Yahweh in some way. He uses many tactics for this. One of them is to create doubt in our minds that Yahweh and his son do not care about us.—2 Chronicles 11:14; James 1:6.

Five centuries later, when Jesus came to the earth, Satan still made the same attempt to prevent Him from becoming the Son of men in any way. For this, he resorted to many tricks. Like spreading false stories about Jesus through religious leaders and others. Many people fell for their words and crucified Jesus as a criminal.—Read Matt. 11:19; Matt. 27:27-31; Mark 14:55, 56; John 8:41-45.

8 Today, the devil's big trick is to keep people from knowing the truth about Jehovah and Jesus. "The father of lies spreads lies through false religions." (John 8:44) Just as he blinded people’s eyes through Christianity so they wouldn’t know Jehovah and his Son, (2 Corinthians 4:3, 4) churches often teach that the Father and the Son are one and the same, which keeps people from knowing the Father. They don’t know who he is or what his name is. Instead, they worship the Son. But the truth is that it’s completely wrong from Jehovah’s and Jesus’ viewpoint. (Matthew 4:10; John 4:23) Because the devil has taught them lies, they can’t understand the truth and sometimes even oppose us.

If we listen to the devil's words, we can drift away from Jehovah. A sister named Shainan says, "I used to learn certain things at school and spend time with certain people, and they had a great impact on me. I didn't realize that I started thinking like them. What Jehovah considers wrong began to seem right to me. I was spending too much time on social media, which made me want to be like those people and think like them. Gradually, I moved away from Jehovah, my family, and my church brothers and sisters." It took some time, but Shainan managed to escape the devil's trap and returned to her father, Jehovah. How did she do this?

If we study the Bible in depth, our confidence will grow that Jehovah and Jesus are on our side. (Prov. 22:19) Reflect on the stories that show how much Jehovah and Jesus care about humans. Then you will feel confident that they are your friends and you can trust them. The Bible contains many such things about Jehovah and Jesus that show how much they love us. For example, Jehovah said: "As a mother shows affection to her children who sip her milk, so I will show affection to my people." (Isa. 49:15) Those who love his name, he considers as his "precious possession." (Ps. 3:16, 17, FTR) And Jesus said that he loves humans so much that he is ready even to give up his life for them.—John 15:12, 13.
How has Satan presented the wrong image of Jehovah and Jesus over the years?

All the difficulties that come upon us do not directly come from the devil. But it is the hand of the "nature of this world" behind which the devil is at work. He tempts people to think and act like him, thereby causing them to oppress God's people. So whenever difficulties come upon us or we are opposed, in some way the devil is responsible for it.—1 Corinthians 2:12; 1 John 5:19.
But now I am fully convinced that there is a Creator and despite my flaws, He loves me. Let me tell you why this conviction took hold of me and how it has changed my life because of this faith.

I started living in a small village in French Guiana that was nestled among the jungles. When I was a soldier, this very village was my base. I thought I would live among nature, smoke ganja, and have fun, maybe this would make me happy. But after some time, my life became like it was before. I worked hard the whole week so that I could have fun on Saturdays and Sundays.

We thought that our way of living was the best and everyone in the world should live like us. In our society, no one was considered superior or inferior. Everyone respected each other, whether they belonged to any country or community. But then I felt that everyone thinks only about themselves and there are shortcomings in all of us. Gradually, the same problems arose between us that people everywhere face. Some people stayed there for just a few days, while some stayed for months or even years. I stayed there for two years.

I feel that when I started praying, the Creator paid attention to me and saw that I wanted to know more about Him. There was a girl in our society who was my good friend. She had met Jehovah's Witnesses and they gave her the book "Paradise on Earth where you can live forever." When I read it, I kept reading. I was very happy to learn that the earth would become paradise and we could live here forever. This is what I was looking for! To live on earth in such an atmosphere with them, where there is peace among everyone and no fear of death. I wanted to get closer to that Creator who has promised us such a good life.

I continued studying the Bible and started making changes in my life. I decided that I would stop smoking and taking drugs. So, at that time, I burned all the tobacco and drugs I had, and never touched them again. I also attended some meetings. After one meeting, I asked a brother to cut my long hair, and he did it right there in the royal palace.

My sister in my family was incredibly beautiful, her name was Claudine. I noticed that she enthusiastically promotes Jehovah and it is clear from her responses how much she loves Jehovah. I wanted to date her. But first, I asked her if she wanted to serve as a missionary. She said yes! So we got married in April 2000.

I am facing another difficulty. Since my childhood, I have been suffering from an illness that causes me to sweat a lot, especially in my hands. When I feel tension, the condition worsens even more. For instance, when I have to deliver speeches in front of many people at meetings and sessions, I get extremely nervous. But when I pray for peace of mind, it makes a significant difference. My illness hasn't completely gone away, but trusting in Yahwea helps me remain calm and reduces my anxiety.

When I first attended the assembly, I learned that our great Creator Jehovah always cares about his people. Giving me the first place in life has truly blessed me with many gifts. Jehovah taught me to be humble and respect those in authority. I broke off friendships with those who did not measure up to Jehovah's level, but Jehovah has given me many good friends. Jehovah gave me a wonderful wife. He also gave me a beautiful hope. I am eagerly waiting for that time when we all will live forever in the new world and receive even more blessings from Jehovah.—Mr. 10:29, 30.
Delivering a speech in front of a group speaking Chinese, 2006

We do not wage war as Yahwea's servants. (2 Sam. 2:4; Matt. 18:36) But the Bible does speak about a battle that we all must fight. Our battle is against wicked spirits. (Read Eph. 6:11, 12.) They are more powerful than us, but we can still win against them. For this, we need to trust Yahwea most of all. At the same time, we also need to recognize those practices that Satan and his spirits carry out against us and our brothers and sisters.

Note how King Saul began to hate David. At first, Saul really liked David. David was a very good warrior, so Saul was very happy with him. (1 Sam. 18:5) But when he saw that people were praising David more than him, it did not sit well with him at all. He began to hate David so much that he tried to kill him. (1 Sam. 18:9-11) If David had been killed by Saul’s hands, the devil would have been overjoyed because God’s purpose would not be fulfilled. How so? God had already chosen David to be the next king of Israel. (1 Sam. 16:13) Just think about it, how much fun the devil must be having watching Saul, who is hating David, end up valuing David’s life as much as God wanted him to value it.

When a brother or sister does something that offends you, remember that you too are incomplete and make many mistakes. When we serve Jehovah together with our brothers and sisters, we see each other's faults more clearly. (Ps. 7:20) When this happens, follow Jehovah’s advice. Be patient with one another and be ready to forgive. (Col. 3:12-14) Jehovah and Jesus want us to always maintain unity in this family of brothers and sisters. Give them your full support in this purpose. —John 17:20, 21.

After many centuries, when the promised Messiah, Jesus, came to the earth, a lot went wrong with him too. Like some of his relatives said that his mind had gone back. (Mark 3:21) Religious teachers said that Jesus was using evil angels to heal people and had no right to teach them. (Luke 11:15, 16) One of his close ones betrayed him. (Matthew 26:14-16) The chief priests colluded with other officials to sentence him to death. (Mark 15:1, 13-15) So much opposition was faced by Jesus, yet he did not waver from serving Yahweh, nor did he ever consider changing. When Jesus was arrested, Peter wanted to fight on his behalf. He drew a sword at the high priest’s servant and cut off his ear, but Jesus did not approve. He healed the servant’s ear through a miracle. (Luke 22:50, 51) On all these occasions, Jesus did not divert his attention from serving Yahwe, nor did he ever consider changing.

If we try to eradicate the evils in the world even a million times, it will be of no use. Such an endeavor is merely a waste of time and strength. (Ps. 1:15) Yahweh knows what has passed over us. (Ps. 37:18) Soon He will bring His kingdom to earth, and Satan and his angels will repair whatever damage they have caused. (1 John 3:8; Rev. 21:5) But until then, we must endure and love the most. We need to invest our time and strength in spreading the message so that as many people as possible become friends of Yahweh.

Paul may have wondered what Philippians would do when Onesimus returned to him. Philippians could legally punish Onesimus. But the question was, would he do it? If he did, how would that affect the church? Would there be division among brothers who worked as masters or slaves and served in the same church? Paul knew this wasn't a small matter because it could disrupt the peace. So, Paul wrote a letter to Philippians and entrusted it to Tychikos to deliver. (Philemon 6:21, 22; Colossians 4:7-9) At the same time, Paul also sent a letter for the Colossian church. Let's see what we can learn from what is said about Paul, Onesimus, and Philemon in these letters.

Paul commended Philemon. (Philem. 4, 5, 7) It is right to commend each person. Why? Because we all think about and fear certain things. For example, we might worry about our skin color or how we look, or what others think of us, causing us to be anxious. Or we might fear that if time comes when we have to forsake our duty to Yahweh in service, what will happen. Such thoughts can arise in any person’s mind. But if we dwell on these matters, we may become overly anxious, easily dissatisfied, suspicious, or try to appear better than others. This could disrupt the peace of the community. When we are fearful or anxious, if a brother or sister commends us, it will surely make us feel good! (Heb. 12:25) From this, we are even more convinced that others value us and see us as valuable. Don’t you want others to be encouraged through your words? So, seek opportunities to commend others from the heart. Do not commend others only for their good deeds, but also for the effort they put in. In other words, whenever you see something good, speak well of it.

10 Often we say or do things that could make others feel bad. How can we maintain peace in such situations? We can learn much from Philemon on this matter. He did something that seems easy to hear but is very difficult to do. Philemon admitted his mistake and reconciled with his fellow Christian, Tychicus. Philemon knew according to Roman law he had to return to his master. So, he spent a lot of money and traveled about 1400 kilometers to return to his master and face the consequences of his actions, including becoming a slave again. It was certainly not an easy thing for him to do. Think about it, if Philemon had thought to himself that he had not made any mistake by running away from his master, then returning to his master would have been even more difficult! But still, for the sake of reconciliation, he returned to his master, who was now not just his owner but also his brother.

Philippians loved his brothers and sisters (Phil. 5). Philippians means "full of love," and he lived up to this name. Every member of the Colossian church knew that Philippians loved everyone. This is perhaps why he was able to forgive Onesimus. In his letter to the Colossians, Paul wrote, "Love is what makes all people completely one." (Read Colossians 3:14.) In other words, love is very important for maintaining peace and unity. The more we love others, the easier it becomes to forgive them and treat them with love. (1 Corinthians 13:4-7) Now let's see how Philippians increased his love.

When Paul said, "Bear one another’s burdens," he was really getting at what? He said that when brothers and sisters irritate us or cause us distress, we can still maintain patience toward them and act with love. At the same place, Paul also gave Yahweh as an example. Yahweh does not expect too much from his servants. He knows that we make mistakes because we are not perfect. But even so, he focuses on our good qualities. This is why he always shows great kindness to us and forgives us. (Psalm 103:13, 14; 130:3) Therefore, if we view our brothers and sisters as Yahweh does, it will become much easier for us to tolerate their faults. We can be patient with them just as Yahweh is patient with us and tolerates our mistakes. Think about an example to understand this. When we remember how beautiful flowers bloom on a tree, we also take care of the tree when no flowers are blooming. Similarly, if we remember that there are many good qualities among our brothers and sisters, we can forgive them and show love to them even when they cause us pain.
When Paul sent Onesimus to Philemon, he might have thought about certain matters (see the image for the picture).

Why is love important for keeping peace? (Colossians 3:14)

Merchants sold goods there. It is thought that goods were sold near the gate of some city in Jerusalem, and the gate was named after the goods sold there. For example, Fish Gate and Sheep Gate.—Jas. 1:10; John 5:2.

People were taught to rely on Yahweh. Preachers and others would proclaim messages at the city gates because many people gathered there. (1 Kings 22:10; Jeremiah 17:19, 20) For example, Jehu proclaimed before all the people at the city gate that everything he had said against the family of Ahab had come to pass. (2 Kings 10:8-10) King Hezekiah gathered his army officers at the city gate and encouraged them to rely on Yahweh. —2 Chronicles 32:6-8.

From the day we decide to serve Yahweh, Satan and his evil angels become our enemies. Satan knows well that as long as we remain close to Yahweh and maintain trust in Him, he cannot harm us. Therefore, he constantly tries to make us distance ourselves from Yahweh. To do this, he uses various tricks. One of them is trying to create doubt in our minds about whether Yahweh and His Son care for us at all. —2 Corinthians 11:14; James 1:6.

After five years, when Jesus came to the earth, Satan’s effort was still to prevent people from becoming his disciples in any way possible. For this, he used various tricks. For example, Satan spread lies about Jesus through religious leaders and other individuals. Many people believed these lies and had Jesus killed as a criminal. —Read, Matthew 11:19; 27:27-31; Mark 14:55, 56; John 8:41-45.

Currently, Satan is using this trick so that people cannot know the truth about Yahweh and Jesus. "The father of lies" Satan uses false religions to spread lies about them. (John 8:44) For example, through Christian circles, Satan has blinded people so they cannot know the truth about Yahweh and his son. (2 Cor. 4:3, 4) It is often taught in churches that the Father and the Son are one. This is why people do not know the Father. They do not know who he is or what his name is. On the other hand, they worship the Son. But from Yahweh and Jesus' perspective, this is completely wrong. (Matt. 4:10; John 4:23) Satan has blinded people, so they cannot understand the truth and sometimes even oppose us.

12 If we listen to Satan's words, we might end up distancing ourselves from Yahweh. A niece named Shannon says, "The things I learned at school and the people I interacted with had a negative influence on me. I couldn't understand when I started thinking like them. From Yahweh's perspective, what was wrong, I kept thinking it was right. I spent so much time behind social media that I felt as if I was becoming like them and thinking like them. Gradually, I moved away from Yahweh, my family, and my church members." It took some time, but the niece Shannon managed to break free from Satan's trap and return to Yahweh. How did she do it?

If we deeply study the Bible, our faith on this matter will grow stronger that Jehovah and Jesus are with us. (Heb. 13:21) Think deeply about these details from which we can understand how much Jehovah and Jesus care for humanity. As a result, you can be sure that they are your friends and you can trust them. The Bible contains such statements about Jehovah and Jesus that show how much they love us. For example, Jehovah says that as a mother loves her nursing child, Jehovah loves his people even more. (Isa. 49:15) Those who love his name, Jehovah considers them his "special treasure." (Mal. 3:16, 17, Common Language Version) And Jesus said that he loves people so much that he is willing to give up his own life for them.—John 15:12, 13.
How did Satan spread false notions about Yahweh and Jesus in the past?

All the problems that come upon us do not directly come from Satan. But behind this 'worldly thinking,' Satan's hand is also there. Satan gives people the thoughts and actions similar to his own, causing them to persecute God's people. Therefore, whenever we face any problem or are opposed, in some way, Satan is responsible for it.—1 Corinthians 2:12; 1 John 5:19.
But now I have come to understand that there is a Creator who cares for me despite my various weaknesses. Let me tell you how my thinking and life have been turned around.

I moved to a small village in French Guiana, which was located in the middle of a rainforest. Previously, I worked in the army. I thought that if I stayed in nature, smoked marijuana, and enjoyed life as I pleased, maybe I could be happy. But after some time, I realized that my life had become just like before. I worked the whole week so that I could party at the end of the week.

We lived our lives the way we wanted, and we aspired for the whole world to be that way too. No one in our group had authority over anyone else, and we respected each other, wherever our stage might be. However, later I came to understand that we all initially think about ourselves first and we all make mistakes. Such problems exist in our lives too, which others are facing as well. Some of us were part of this group for a few days, while many stayed for a few weeks or months. But I was associated with this group for more than two years.

I think when I started praying, God noticed me and understood that I wanted to know more about Him. We met a friend from our group who showed us Yahweh's testimonies. They gave him a book named "An Everlasting Presence on Earth." When I started reading the book, I was completely amazed! The hope of everlasting presence on Earth filled my heart with joy. I wanted exactly such a world where I could stay in peace with my loved ones and never die. I also wanted to be even closer to my generous Creator who has planned such an unprecedented future for us.

I learn various topics from the Bible and realize that there needs to be some changes in my life. I decide to quit smoking and stop using marijuana. After making this decision, I burn all the tobacco and marijuana I had and have never used them again. I start attending a few meetings. In one meeting, I tell a brother to cut my long hair, which he did, as he had cut my hair for me in the kingdom.

There was a beautiful daughter named Clidine in my family, whom I liked very much. I noticed that she was very enthusiastic about evangelism, and from her comments in gatherings, I understood that she loved Yahweh very much. I wanted to date her. But before that, I wanted to know if Clidine was also eager to serve as a missionary. She was eager. We got married in April 2000.

I had another issue as well. Since childhood, I had suffered from hyperhidrosis, which made me sweat excessively. Especially, my palms would sweat a lot. This problem worsened at times when I felt a lot of pressure, such as when presenting on a topic in front of an audience. But when I sought peace in Yahweh, this problem lessened significantly for me. However, even now, I still have this issue, but the more I rely on Yahweh, the more peaceful I can be, and consequently, my sweating decreases.

I can learn at my first assembly that our great Creator always cares for His worshippers. And since I have placed serving Yahweh first, He has blessed me abundantly. Yahweh has helped me to maintain the right attitude toward the leadership and to be gentle. According to Yahweh's value, I have given up socializing with the world's friends but He has given me true friends. Besides, He has given me a very good wife. I am looking forward to that time when we will enjoy eternal life forever and Yahweh will bless us generously.—Mark 10:29, 30.
(Directory) Giving a lecture in Chinese in a group on the right side in 2006

As servants of Yahweh, we do not take part in wars (Isaiah 2:4; John 18:36). But the Bible speaks of a war where all of us will have to participate. Our war or battle is against evil angels of the bad heavens. (Read Ephesians 6:11, 12.) Although they are much stronger than us, we can still win this battle. First and foremost, we need to rely on Yahweh. Besides, we need to identify the tricks and deceptions that Satan and his evil angels use against us and our brothers and sisters.

Think about why King Saul began to hate David. At first, Saul really liked David. David was a brave warrior, and Saul was very pleased with him. (1 Sam. 18:5) But when Saul saw that people were praising David more than him, he could not accept it. Saul started to treat David so cruelly that he even began jumping up and down, wanting to kill him. (1 Sam. 18:9-11) If David had died at Saul's hands, Satan would have been very happy because it would have thwarted Yahweh's purpose. Why? Because long ago, Yahweh had chosen David to be the next king of Israel. (1 Sam. 16:13) Consider this: how happy Satan must have been at that time, watching Saul, who had become violent, jump up and down, wanting to kill the person whom Yahweh wanted to appoint as the next king of Israel.

8 When a brother or sister does something that causes you pain, remember that you too are sometimes unfruitful. You also make mistakes from time to time. When we serve Yahweh together with our brothers and sisters, we can more clearly see their faults. (James 7:20) When this happens, follow Yahweh’s advice. Be patient toward each other and make every effort to maintain unity. (Colossians 3:12-14) Yahweh and Jesus want there to always be unity among our brothers and sisters. Fully support their goal of unity. —John 17:20, 21.

When the promised Messiah Jesus came to the earth after many years, he too became a victim of injustice. For instance, some of Jesus' relatives said that his mind had gone wrong. (Mark 3:21) The religious leaders claimed that Jesus healed people with the help of evil spirits and had no authority to teach. (Luke 11:15, 16) One of Jesus' close friends betrayed him. (Matthew 26:14-16) The chief priests and teachers gathered together to persecute Jesus and declared that he should be sentenced to death. (Mark 15:1, 13-15) Despite all this injustice towards Jesus, he never turned away from serving Yahweh or thought about taking revenge. When Jesus was arrested, his father wanted to fight for him. He struck one of the high priests and cut off his ear, but it did not seem right to Jesus. He miraculously restored the ear of that servant. (Luke 22:50, 51) In such circumstances, Jesus never diverted his attention from serving Yahwe, nor did he ever think about taking revenge.

15 We may try a hundred times, but we will never be able to eliminate injustice from this earth. Trying to do so would only waste our time and strength. (Heb. 1:15) But Yahweh knows that we are passing through various circumstances. (Ps. 37:18) Very soon, when Yahweh comes to take His kingdom on earth, He will restore all the damage done by Satan and wicked heavenly messengers. (1 John 3:8; Rev. 21:5) But until that time comes, we must endure patiently and love everyone. And we must spend our time and strength in the work of spreading the gospel so that more people can become Yahweh’s friends.

How should we behave towards those who oppose and harass us? (Matthew 5:43, 44)

"I prefer to plead with you out of love."—FLM. 9.

How would Filemon react if Onesimus returned? Would Filemon impose a heavy punishment on him, in accordance with his rights as a master? How would the congregation react? Would brothers and sisters who were masters or slaves clash over this issue? Paul knew that such a situation could disrupt the peace in the congregation. For that reason, he wrote a letter to Filemon and sent it through a brother named Tychicus. (Eph. 6:21, 22; Col. 4:7-9) At the same time, Paul also wrote a letter to the congregation in Colosse. Let's discuss what we can learn from these two letters about Paul, Onesimus, and Filemon.
